advances: An ordinary-volume optimization inside a fixed projection. The full inherited boundary flux remains and does not give a mixed-integer depth estimate.

proof:
The lower bound on each offset is exactly the containment condition. An offset exceeding $h_P(a_i)$ is redundant and can be clipped to that bound. If an integer point belongs to the interior at a limiting parameter, it is in $\operatorname{int}P$ and strictly satisfies each of the finitely many cuts. It would be interior at all sufficiently close parameters. Feasibility is therefore closed. For $b^{(j)}\to b$, the sets $L(b^{(j)})$ are eventually contained in $L(b)+\epsilon B_2^n$ for each $\epsilon>0$: otherwise a convergent subsequence of violating points in $P$ would limit to a point satisfying all cuts. Taking the volume upper limit and then decreasing $\epsilon$ to zero gives upper semicontinuity even if the limiting volume is zero. The nonempty feasible parameter box is compact.

For a genuine facet, move its owner (all copies of the same inequality, if present) outward by a small positive amount. The plane cuts $\operatorname{int}P$, so there is slack to $h_P(a_i)$. Relative-interior points of the facet have strict slack in the other distinct planes; points of its relative boundary in $\operatorname{int}P$ are on at least one other plane. Containment of $K$ persists, and a prism over a small relative ball in $\operatorname{relint}F_i\cap\operatorname{int}P$ gives a strictly positive volume gain. The integer points of $P$ are finite. Those on $\partial P$ or an unchanged cut, or strictly violating an unchanged cut, cannot become interior. Any point strictly violating the moved cut retains that strict violation for a sufficiently small motion, uniformly over the finite set of such points. Without a witness on the genuine facet relative interior these cases cover the entire lattice census, contradicting maximality. With a witness the same slack argument places it in the interior for the simultaneous outward homothetic motion.

Up to surface-null sets the boundary is the disjoint union of $\Gamma_P$ and the genuine cut facets. Intersections of different planes have surface measure zero. If a cut plane meets $\operatorname{int}P$, its intersection with $\partial P$ is the relative boundary of the planar section, also surface null. Any supporting cut plane is redundant on $P$, and has no separate moving portion. The outward normal on the inherited part agrees almost everywhere with $n_P$. Gauss–Green for the convex body's Lipschitz boundary, applied to constant coordinate fields and to $(z_k-q_k)e_j$, gives the vector and matrix identities. Taking the trace gives the scalar identity. The supporting distance of an inherited plane from $q$ is at least the radius of any ball centered at $q$ contained in $L$; the same distance is positive on a genuine cut. At a witness only the normal coordinate $a_i\cdot p_i=b_i$ is determined, so the substitution is valid in the scalar identity.

For the derivatives, change the moving inequalities one at a time at fixed $t$ and telescope. In coordinates $z=w+s a_i$ with $a_i\cdot w=b_i$, the changed strip lies in $|s|\le C|t|$ on a fixed bounded neighborhood of $P$. Under the affine motion the new boundary is $s=t\,a_i\cdot(Bw+v)+O(t^2)$ uniformly there, by applying $(I+tB)^{-1}$ to the moved inequality. In an offset motion it is exactly the offset displacement. For almost every $w$ in that plane, either $w\in\operatorname{int}P$ and all other cut inequalities are strict, or $w$ lies strictly outside $P$ or violates an unchanged limiting cut. The exceptions on the plane are surface null by the preceding boundary argument; identical owners are treated together. In the first case the signed swept length divided by $t$ tends to the prescribed normal speed, and in the second case to zero. Dominated convergence proves the sum of facet speed integrals, including for two-sided $t$ and any mix of expanding and contracting facets. Integrating the affine speed over each facet gives $A_i a_i\cdot(Bc_i+v)$. Gauss–Green on the full boundary for $Bz+v$ gives the other expression. The offset speed gives the scalar derivative above. Inward motion of a redundant plane coincident with a positive-area inherited face would add a one-sided term and is outside the stated deformations.
statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a compact convex body, $K\subset P$ nonempty compact, and $a_1,\ldots,a_N$ fixed unit vectors. For $L(b)=P\cap\bigcap_i\{z:a_i\cdot z\le b_i\}$, maximize ordinary $n$-volume subject to $K\subset L(b)$ and $\operatorname{int}L(b)\cap\mathbb Z^n=\varnothing$. If feasible, the maximum is attained with $h_K(a_i)\le b_i\le h_P(a_i)$, where $h_D(a)=\max_{z\in D}a\cdot z$. At a positive-volume maximum, each genuine cut facet $F_i=L\cap\{a_i\cdot z=b_i\}$ whose relative interior lies in $\operatorname{int}P$ has $p_i\in\operatorname{relint}F_i\cap\operatorname{int}P\cap\mathbb Z^n$, so $b_i=a_i\cdot p_i$. Identical active cuts have one common facet owner.

For any positive-volume $L=L(b)$ in this class, write $A_i=\mathcal H^{n-1}(F_i)$ and $c_i$ for its genuine cut facet areas and centroids. Write $\Gamma_P=\partial L\cap\partial P$, with outward unit normal $n_P(z)$ almost everywhere; integrals on it use $\mathcal H^{n-1}$. For $q\in\operatorname{int}L$,
$$
\sum_i A_i a_i+\int_{\Gamma_P}n_P=0,\qquad
\sum_i A_i a_i(c_i-q)^{\mathsf T}+\int_{\Gamma_P}n_P(z)(z-q)^{\mathsf T}=|L|I_n.
$$
In particular, with $\Phi_P(q)=\int_{\Gamma_P}(z-q)\cdot n_P(z)$,
$$
n|L|=\sum_i A_i(b_i-a_i\cdot q)+\Phi_P(q).
$$
All the scalar contributions are nonnegative; $\Phi_P(q)>0$ if $\Gamma_P$ has positive surface measure. At a maximum each scalar offset can be replaced by $a_i\cdot p_i$, without a centroid identity.

Moving only genuine cut planes by $b_i(t)=b_i+t(b_i-a_i\cdot q)$, keeping $P$ fixed, gives volume derivative $n|L|-\Phi_P(q)$. The outward path is infeasible for interior lattice exclusion at a maximum having a genuine facet. More generally, physically move the genuine planes by $z\mapsto z+t(Bz+v)$ for fixed $B,v$, still clipping to fixed $P$ and keeping any other planes fixed. The volume derivative is
$$
\sum_i A_i a_i\cdot(Bc_i+v)=|L|\operatorname{tr}B-\int_{\Gamma_P}n_P(z)\cdot(Bz+v).
$$
This affine motion does not assert admissibility in the fixed-normal optimization. A cut coincident with an inherited positive-area face is counted only in $\Gamma_P$; the formulas move no such cut.
title: Attained fixed-direction relative lattice-free containers and boundary flux
